rationale: Clear beat-and-raise: EPS $2.80 vs $2.29, raised full-year guidance to $12-13B EBIT-adjusted, $9.75-$10.50 EPS. Mary/Paul directly state 2026 will be 'even better than 2025'. Multiple specific levers: expanded MSRP tariff offset (gross tariff exposure cut $500M), 35% tariff mitigation, 15% YoY share count reduction via $3.5B YTD buybacks, China profitable 4 consecutive quarters, 17% US market share (highest Q3 since 2017), Super Cruise subs nearly doubled YoY. Direct, specific Q&A answers. Tempering factors keep this at 4 rather than 5: $1.6B special charge (EV restructuring, BrightDrop shutdown), $900M YoY warranty headwind management calls 'too high', NA margins only 6.2% (still below 8-10% target), China chip supply risk flagged as fluid, EV demand softening post-credit. Beat-and-raise with real balance-sheet pain acknowledged.

Exceptional momentum. First-ever $100B quarter, revenue +16%, Cloud +34% (accelerating), Cloud backlog +82% YoY to $155B (+$49B sequential), Services +14%, Search +15%, YouTube ads +15%. More $1B+ Cloud deals in 9 months of 2025 than prior 2 years combined. GCP new customers +34% YoY. Gemini at 650M MAUs with queries 3x QoQ. AI Mode at 75M DAU driving incremental query growth. Ex-EC-fine operating margin expanded to 33.9% and op income +22%. Cloud op margin 17.1%→23.7%. Raised 2025 CapEx to $91-93B (from $85B), signaled 'significant increase' in 2026 CapEx on customer demand — a confidence signal, not defensive. Direct Q&A: specific forward catalysts (Gemini 3 launch, Ironwood TPU GA, Anthropic 1M TPU deal, Waymo London/Tokyo 2026, Android XR launch). Depreciation acceleration is the only margin drag and it's a demand-driven problem. Strong conviction momentum continues.

Thin EPS beat ($0.58 vs $0.50) masking clearly softening outlook. Q4 NA revenue guided -12% to -13% sequentially, 2026 CapEx cut ~30% to ~$1B (a major de-risking signal), $284M severance/write-offs taken to 'reset cost structure' (labor savings ~$100M/qtr starting Q4), $125M tax valuation allowance. CEO describes NA as 'a tough market today' and 2026 as 'overall flattish'. International revenue -2% YoY, Middle East Saudi Arabia weak. Stacked fleets 'probably don't come back to work'. Management language is hedging: 'timing and shape remain uncertain', OPEC+ barrels entering market, Mexico declining, NA 'below maintenance level spend'. VoltaGrid/AI power optionality and Oracle 2.3GW deal are real positives but distant, project-level, small vs core OFS drag. $23M Argentina impairment and $31M tariff hit rising to $60M in Q4. Defensive, not offensive — classic softening-growth setup despite the headline beat.

Record Q3 with beat-and-raise elements: EPS $3.68 vs $3.29, record revenue $3.2B (+16.1% YoY), shipbuilding +18%, Ingalls +24.7%, Newport News +14.5% with margin dramatically improving (1.1%→4.9% YoY), Mission Technologies +11% with 1.25x book-to-bill. Raised shipbuilding and Mission Tech revenue guidance by $50M at midpoint each, raised FCF guidance to $550-650M (up $50M). Dividend raised to $1.38. $56B backlog ($33B funded). 4,600 shipbuilders hired YTD with retention improving post-wage investment. Shipbuilding explicitly prioritized in shutdown guidance — no impact. Strong forward catalysts: CVN-79 Kennedy sea trials around year-end, SSN 798 delivery this year, Shield AI/Babcock/Thales partnerships, ROMULUS USV program. Tempering factors keep this at 4 rather than 5: had to trim 2025 throughput improvement expectation (slower start to year), Block VI and Columbia Build II awards timing is uncertain — if slip to 2026 would push shipbuilding margin below midpoint (explicit guidance risk called out), negative $13M cumulative adjustment at NNS, modest FCF ($16M in Q) and '25/'26 cumulative target only $1.2B. Solid setup with identifiable timing risk — more positive than negative.
